final_candidates.decision_summary: D342 showed the highest AlphaMissense pathogenicity score among tested positions (z=0.173 for D342A). The conservative D342N substitution disrupts a critical aspartate likely involved in catalysis or metal coordination while preserving structural viability.
D342A directly demonstrated the highest pathogenicity score (z=0.173) among all tested mutations, indicating strong potential for loss-of-function at this catalytically important aspartate residue.

Charge reversal at E429 in the catalytic domain is highly disruptive to local electrostatics and likely abolishes enzymatic activity. E429A showed low pathogenicity (z=0.082), but the more drastic charge reversal to lysine is expected to be more deleterious.
